items.stem: If two positive integers p and q can be expressed as p = 18a²b⁴ and q = 20a³b², where a and b are prime numbers, then LCM (p, q) is
items.answer:
LCM is the product of the greatest power of each prime factor involved in the numbers.
p = 18a²b⁴ = 2 × 3 × 3 × a × a × b × b × b × b
q = 20a³b² = 2 × 2 × 5 × a × a × a × b × b
LCM(p, q) = 2 × 2 × 3 × 3 × 5 × a³ × b⁴ = 180a³b⁴
Thus (d) is the correct option.
items.concept: HCF and LCM by prime factorisation

Thus (c) is the correct option.

items.stem: The sum of exponents of prime factors in the prime-factorisation of 196 is
items.answer:
196 = 4 × 49 = 2² × 7².
The sum of the exponents of the prime factors is 2 + 2 = 4.
Thus (b) is the correct option.

items.stem: The LCM of the smallest two digit composite number and the smallest composite number is
items.answer:
The smallest two digit composite number is 10 and the smallest composite number is 4.
LCM(10, 4) = 20
Thus (c) is the correct option.

items.stem: HCF of two numbers is 27 and their LCM is 162. If one of the numbers is 54, then the other number is
items.answer:
Let y be the second number. The product of two numbers equals the product of their LCM and HCF.
54 × y = LCM × HCF
54 × y = 162 × 27
y = (162 × 27)/54 = 81
Thus (d) is the correct option.

items.stem: HCF of 144 and 198 is
items.answer:
Using the prime factorisation method,
144 = 2 × 2 × 2 × 2 × 3 × 3 = 2⁴ × 3²
198 = 2 × 3 × 3 × 11 = 2 × 3² × 11
HCF(144, 198) = 2 × 3² = 2 × 9 = 18
Thus (b) is the correct option.

items.stem: 2√3 is
items.answer:
Let us assume that 2√3 is a rational number.
Then 2√3 = r, where r is rational, so √3 = r/2.
But √3 is irrational, so r/2 would have to be irrational to make the equation true. This contradicts the assumption that r is rational.
Hence our assumption is wrong and 2√3 is an irrational number.
Thus (c) is the correct option.
items.concept: Definition of an irrational number

items.stem: The product of a non-zero rational number and an irrational number is
items.answer:
The product of a non-zero rational number and an irrational number is always irrational. For example, (3/4) × √2 = 3√2/4, which is irrational.
Thus (a) is the correct option.

items.stem: If two positive integers a and b are written as a = x³y² and b = xy³, where x, y are prime numbers, then HCF (a, b) is
items.answer:
a = x³y² = x × x × x × y × y
b = xy³ = x × y × y × y
HCF is the product of the smallest power of each common prime factor.
HCF(a, b) = x × y × y = xy²
Thus (b) is the correct option.

items.stem: If two positive integers p and q can be expressed as p = ab² and q = a³b, where a, b are prime numbers, then LCM (p, q) is equal to
items.answer:
p = ab² = a × b × b
q = a³b = a × a × a × b
LCM is the product of the greatest power of each prime factor involved.
LCM(p, q) = a³ × b² = a³b²
Thus (c) is the correct option.

items.stem: If p₁ and p₂ are two odd prime numbers such that p₁ > p₂, then p₁² − p₂² is
items.answer:
p₁² − p₂² is an even number.
Take p₁ = 5 and p₂ = 3. Then p₁² − p₂² = 25 − 9 = 16, which is an even number.
Thus (a) is the correct option.

items.stem: The number 3¹³ − 3¹⁰ is divisible by
items.answer:
3¹³ − 3¹⁰ = 3¹⁰(3³ − 1) = 3¹⁰ × 26 = 2 × 13 × 3¹⁰
Hence 3¹³ − 3¹⁰ is divisible by 2, 3 and 13.
Thus (d) is the correct option.

items.stem: 1. The L.C.M. of x and 18 is 36. 2. The H.C.F. of x and 18 is 2. What is the number x?
items.answer:
LCM × HCF = first number × second number.
So the required number x = (36 × 2)/18 = 4.
Thus (d) is the correct option.

items.stem: If a = 2³ × 3, b = 2 × 3 × 5, c = 3ⁿ × 5 and LCM (a, b, c) = 2³ × 3² × 5, then n is
items.answer:
The LCM takes the greatest power of each prime. The greatest power of 3 in the LCM is 3², but a and b each contribute only 3¹, so the 3² must come from c = 3ⁿ × 5. Hence n = 2.
Thus (b) is the correct option.

items.stem: The least number which is a perfect square and is divisible by each of 16, 20 and 24 is
items.answer:
The LCM of 16, 20 and 24 is 240. The least multiple of 240 that is a perfect square is 3600. Choices (a) 240 and (c) 2400 can be eliminated at once because they are not perfect squares, and 1600 is not a multiple of 240.
Thus (d) is the correct option.

items.stem: Assertion (A): The HCF of two numbers is 5 and their product is 150, then their LCM is 30. Reason (R): For any two positive integers a and b, HCF (a, b) + LCM (a, b) = a × b.
items.assertion: The HCF of two numbers is 5 and their product is 150, then their LCM is 30.
items.reason: For any two positive integers a and b, HCF (a, b) + LCM (a, b) = a × b.

options.label: A
options.text: Both assertion (A) and reason (R) are true and reason (R) is the correct explanation of assertion (A).

options.label: B

options.label: C

options.text: Assertion (A) is false but reason (R) is true.

items.answer:
The correct relation is LCM(a, b) × HCF(a, b) = a × b, not a sum, so the reason is false.
Checking the assertion: LCM × 5 = 150, so LCM = 150/5 = 30. The assertion is true.
Assertion (A) is true but reason (R) is false.
Thus (c) is the correct option.
